title: Evaluate an implementation-partner channel for Zedu institutional adoption
description: Research whether education technology consultants and training operations agencies can help institutions evaluate and implement Zedu. Distinct from creators, newsletter co-marketing and campus ambassadors: these partners would provide buyer implementation services. Deliver a sourced shortlist of ten organisations, qualification criteria, potential service boundaries, a discovery-question set and a small pilot design. Verify current services from public business sources; do not imply endorsement or partnership. Done when the team approves go/defer criteria and a pilot with responsibilities, buyer protections and measures of qualified introductions and successful handoffs. No commissions, exclusivity, contact or agreements without approval.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Draft the partner offer and rules of engagement for team approval before any outreach
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The accepted workstream finds who to partner with. This idea defines what Zedu offers them, so the first conversation is consistent. Approach: draft options for the team to choose from (services-only, referral fee, or reseller), lead registration and conflict rules, the minimum training a partner completes, the support boundary between partner and Zedu, and how a partner-led deployment is checked. Done: a 2-page partner offer draft with the open decisions flagged; nothing is promised to a partner until the team approves it.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Screen for implementers who have deployed a platform, not advisers who recommend one
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Nigeria has many "edtech consultants" who are really trainers, curriculum writers or resellers. A partner channel fails if the shortlist is full of them, because the goal needs someone who can run implementation: migrate a school's cohorts, set up roles and channels, train staff, and hand over cleanly.

Approach: build the ten from public business sources only, with two screens applied before scoring.
Screen 1 - evidence of implementation, not advice. A named education client where the partner's own site describes deployment work (migration, roll-out, training, support), not a logo wall or a testimonial. An organisation that only writes strategy or sells courses is listed as a near-miss with the reason, not quietly dropped.
Screen 2 - conflict check. Does the partner resell or implement a named competing LMS or communication platform? If yes, record it; a partner with a competing product cannot be a neutral implementation channel for Zedu.

Then score each survivor on one page: named institutional clients with links, countries covered, team roles their site actually names, whether they publish an NDPR or data-protection position, and what they could own versus what Zedu keeps.

Deliverable: ten rows with a source link and check date per row, "not published" where a fact is missing rather than a guess; qualification criteria as a scored rubric; a service-boundary table (partner owns migration, training, support handoff; Zedu keeps product, pricing and the commercial relationship); seven discovery questions; and a 90-day pilot design with three institutions, with qualified introduction defined as a booked demo with a named decision maker, plus measures for time to first cohort on Zedu and handoff completeness.

Boundaries: no contact, no commissions, no exclusivity and no implied endorsement before approval. Contact routes are recorded for the approved list only.
